questions.contextText: Summary of Passage (Q.16–20): Ceylon attained political independence very differently from Burma and India—without Japanese occupation, revolutionary upheaval, civil disobedience, or jailed nationalist leaders. Because there was no mass liberation struggle, it also lacked the usual concomitant hardening of national solidarity through sacrifice. Instead, independence came via peaceful negotiations, shaped by deep Westernisation across nearly 450 years of Portuguese, Dutch, and British rule. Missionary and British-style schools—some even emulating English public schools—produced a thoroughly Anglicised, politically conservative elite nicknamed 'brown sahibs'.
